venues.name: Capella Hanoi
venues.area: French Quarter / near the Opera House (Hoan Kiem)
venues.note: Bill Bensley's 1920s opera fantasy, 47 rooms, each a jewel-box, and the finest address in the city.

venues.name: Sofitel Legend Metropole Hanoi
venues.note: The city's grande dame since 1901, colonial white-and-green, and the address every visitor of consequence has passed through.
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide Five-Star (2025, fifth consecutive year)
Condé Nast Traveler Gold List 2025 (only hotel in Vietnam)

venues.name: InterContinental Hanoi Westlake
venues.note: Over-water pavilions on stilts above West Lake, a resort calm rare this close to the centre.

venues.name: JW Marriott Hotel Hanoi
venues.area: Nam Tu Liem / Convention district (west Hanoi)
venues.note: Carlos Zapata's dragon-inspired curve, the capital's grand modern house, chosen for heads of state.

venues.name: Meliá Hanoi
venues.note: A dependable, well-placed international tower in the heart of the city.

venues.name: Apricot Hotel
venues.note: An art-filled boutique house facing Hoan Kiem Lake, Vietnamese paintings on every wall.

venues.name: Peridot Grand Luxury Boutique Hotel
venues.note: A polished, urbane boutique tower in the thick of the Old Quarter.

venues.name: Gia
venues.area: Van Mieu / Dong Da (near the Temple of Literature)
venues.note: A modern love letter to Northern Vietnamese heritage, in an Indochine house opposite the Temple of Literature.

venues.name: Tầm Vị
venues.note: Northern Vietnamese home cooking, kept exact and unhurried, the food a Hanoi grandmother would cook, raised to a star.

venues.name: Hibana by Koki
venues.note: An intimate teppanyaki counter inside Capella, Japanese precision and premium produce, one of the hardest seats in town.

venues.name: ONVIT
venues.area: Yen Hoa / Cau Giay (Grand Plaza Hanoi)
venues.note: Korean fine dining told through Vietnam's finest ingredients, the country's first starred Korean kitchen.

venues.name: Lamai Garden
venues.note: Farm-to-table plant-based cooking with more than half its herbs and vegetables grown on site, a rare green star.

venues.name: Chả Cá Thăng Long
venues.note: Hanoi's signature turmeric-and-dill fish, sizzled at your table over a charcoal brazier, a single, perfect dish.

venues.name: Bún Chả Ta
venues.note: Grilled pork and rice noodles in smoky broth, Hanoi's defining lunch, done properly.

venues.name: Phở Bò Lâm
venues.note: A bowl of beef phở with real conviction, the broth that makes the pilgrimage worth it.

venues.name: Miến Lươn Đông Thịnh
venues.note: Crisp eel and glass noodles, a Hanoi speciality guarded by a single family.

venues.name: Hà Thành Mansion
venues.note: Classic Hanoi cooking in a handsome heritage setting, the old recipes, comfortably staged.

venues.name: Mậu Dịch Số 37
venues.note: Vietnamese comfort food in a nostalgic subsidy-era canteen, a warm plate of the country's recent past.

venues.name: Ưu Đàm Chay
venues.note: Refined vegetarian Vietnamese cooking in a calm, tea-house setting, meat-free without compromise.

venues.name: 1946 Cửa Bắc
venues.note: Authentic regional Vietnamese dishes in an old villa, quiet, generous, of another era.

venues.name: Bún Chả Hương Liên
venues.note: The bún chả joint where Obama and Anthony Bourdain shared a plate and a beer, since immortalised.

venues.name: Phở Gia Truyền Bát Đàn
venues.note: The queue-out-the-door phở the locals line up for at dawn, a legendary bowl and no ceremony.

venues.name: The Old Quarter, the 36 guild streets
venues.note: A thousand years of commerce still hums through this warren north of the lake, where each lane once served a single trade, Hang Bac for silver, Hang Ma for votive paper, Hang Dao for silk. Best walked slowly with a private guide who can read the layers a map cannot.

venues.name: A cyclo ride through the old lanes
venues.note: The gentlest way to take in the crush of the 36 streets, reclined in a pedalled cyclo while the city flows around you, unhurried and eye-level with the shophouses. An easy, charming loop for elders and children alike before the walking begins.

venues.name: Hoan Kiem Lake
venues.note: The green heart of Hanoi and the city's favourite gathering place, its still water wrapped in willows and the legend of the returned sword. A dawn circuit past the red Turtle Tower, when locals practise tai chi, is one of the quietest luxuries the city offers.

venues.name: Ngoc Son Temple & The Huc Bridge
venues.note: A small island temple honouring the general Tran Hung Dao, reached across the vivid vermilion arc of The Huc Bridge. The postcard image of Hanoi, and a serene ten-minute pause in the middle of the old city.

venues.name: Temple of Literature
venues.note: Vietnam's first university, founded in 1070, a series of tranquil walled courtyards, lotus ponds and stelae carried on the backs of stone tortoises. The most composed and contemplative site in the city, and one that resonates with multi-generation families who prize learning.

venues.name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum & Ba Dinh Square
venues.note: The solemn granite mausoleum on the vast ceremonial square where independence was declared in 1945, its changing of the guard a study in precision. A window into the nation's founding story, go early, and dress modestly.

venues.name: One Pillar Pagoda
venues.note: A tiny wooden shrine built in 1049 to resemble a lotus rising on a single stone stem from its pond, tucked within the Ho Chi Minh complex. Small in scale but singular in form, worth the short walk from the mausoleum.

venues.name: Presidential Palace & Ho Chi Minh's stilt house
venues.note: The mustard-yellow French colonial palace with its formal gardens, and behind it the modest teak stilt house where Ho Chi Minh chose to live instead. The contrast between grandeur and simplicity is the whole point.

venues.name: Ho Chi Minh Museum
venues.note: A striking modernist white building beside the mausoleum, its exhibits tracing the life of the leader and the century that shaped modern Vietnam. A cool, orderly stop that completes the Ba Dinh circuit.

venues.name: Imperial Citadel of Thang Long
venues.note: A thousand years of Vietnamese power layered in one place, Ly dynasty palace foundations, colonial gates and the underground command bunker of the American war, all in a single vast enclosure. The archaeological dig alone rewards a private, well-guided morning.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Central Sector of the Imperial Citadel of Thang Long

venues.name: The Old French Quarter
venues.note: Wide tree-lined boulevards, ochre villas and grand hotels laid out during the colonial decades, a world away from the tangle of the Old Quarter. Best explored on foot or by private car, ending with tea at the Metropole where egg coffee was born.

venues.name: Hanoi Opera House
venues.note: A 1911 belle-epoque theatre modelled on the Palais Garnier in Paris, all marble stairs and gilt, still staging opera, ballet and Vietnamese folk concerts. Attend a performance, or simply admire the finest colonial facade in the city.

venues.name: St Joseph's Cathedral
venues.note: A weathered neo-Gothic cathedral from 1886, its twin towers echoing Notre-Dame, presiding over a lively square ringed with cafes. The lanes around it, Nha Tho and Nha Chung, are among the best in the city for a slow coffee and boutique browsing.

venues.name: Vietnam Museum of Ethnology
venues.note: The finest museum in Hanoi, a thoughtful, superbly labelled survey of Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups, with full-scale traditional houses reconstructed in the garden. Genuinely engaging for children and the most rewarding cultural stop in the city.

venues.name: Vietnamese Women's Museum
venues.note: A moving, beautifully curated museum on women in Vietnamese life, marriage, motherhood, war and the street vendors who still carry the city on shoulder poles. Compact, powerful and a short walk south of the lake.

venues.name: Vietnam National Fine Arts Museum
venues.note: Set in an elegant three-storey colonial building, a well-chosen collection running from ancient Buddhist sculpture and lacquer to modern silk painting. Quiet, uncrowded and close to the Temple of Literature.

venues.name: Hoa Lo Prison
venues.note: The remnant of the French colonial prison, later the wartime 'Hanoi Hilton', with unflinching exhibits on both eras. Sobering and well-presented, a serious counterweight to the city's gentler sights.

venues.name: Train Street
venues.note: A famously narrow residential lane where a working train passes within arm's reach of the trackside cafes. Access has been repeatedly restricted for safety and opens and closes without notice, go only with a local guide who knows the day's rules.

venues.name: West Lake (Ho Tay)
venues.note: The city's largest lake, ringed by 17 km of quieter, leafier streets, lakeside villas and the best independent dining in Hanoi. A calm base for a slower stay, with sunset the moment to be on the water's edge.

venues.name: Tran Quoc Pagoda
venues.note: The oldest Buddhist temple in Hanoi, its red brick stupa rising from a slender causeway into West Lake, dating in origin to the 6th century. Loveliest in late afternoon when the light catches the water and incense drifts from the shrine.

venues.name: Quan Thanh Temple
venues.note: A serene 11th-century Taoist temple beside West Lake, guarded by a nearly four-metre bronze statue cast in the 17th century. An easy, atmospheric pairing with Tran Quoc just along the shore.

venues.name: Dong Xuan Market
venues.note: Hanoi's largest covered market, a French-built hall of narrow aisles selling everything from silk and spices to household goods. Chaotic and colourful, a photographer's paradise and a plunge into the working city.

venues.name: Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre
venues.note: A thousand-year-old northern art form performed on a pool of water, lacquered puppets dancing to live traditional music and folk tales of rice farming and dragons. Short, delightful and a sure hit across three generations.

venues.name: Egg coffee (ca phe trung)
venues.note: Hanoi's signature indulgence, whipped egg yolk beaten into a rich sweet cream over strong coffee, invented here in 1946. Cafe Giang, run by the inventor's family, is the original; a hidden upstairs table watching the street is part of the ritual.

venues.name: Old Quarter street-food trail
venues.note: Hanoi is a world capital of street food, pho, bun cha over charcoal, banh cuon, egg coffee, each often mastered by a single family stall. A private evening food guide navigates the crowds, the hygiene and the vegetarian options with ease.

venues.name: Bat Trang ceramics village
venues.note: A 15th-century pottery village 15 km from the centre, its lanes lined with kilns and workshops where you can throw and paint your own piece to be fired and shipped home. A hands-on half-day that delights families and design lovers alike.

venues.name: Long Bien Bridge
venues.note: The great 1902 Eiffel-era iron bridge across the Red River, scarred by war and still carrying trains and cyclists over the water and the banana fields below. A quietly poignant walk at golden hour, away from the tour crowds.

venues.name: Hang Ma & the craft lanes at festival time
venues.note: The lane of votive paper and decorations erupts into colour before Tet and the Mid-Autumn Festival, lanterns and offerings spilling across the street. Timed right, it is one of the most joyous corners of the city.

venues.name: Ba Dinh & the diplomatic quarter by car
venues.note: Beyond the mausoleum, the leafy avenues of embassies, ministries and grand villas make a graceful private drive between the citadel and West Lake. A restful way to link the morning's monuments.

venues.name: Ha Long Bay overnight cruise
venues.note: Nearly 2,000 limestone karsts rising from jade water, best seen from the balcony cabin of a small luxury junk on an overnight sailing, sunset on the sundeck, kayaking hidden lagoons, dawn tai chi. The single most romantic escape from Hanoi, roughly a 2.5-hour transfer away.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Ha Long Bay

venues.name: Lan Ha Bay cruise
venues.note: The quieter, less-visited neighbour of Ha Long off Cat Ba Island, the same soaring karsts and secret beaches, with a fraction of the boats. The connoisseur's choice for an overnight cruise, reached in about three hours.

venues.name: Ninh Binh & Trang An
venues.note: 'Ha Long Bay on land', rowed in a sampan through flooded caves between towering karsts and rice paddies, past ancient temples and the old capital of Hoa Lu. Utterly cinematic, doable as a long day trip or, better, an overnight from Hanoi.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Trang An Landscape Complex

venues.name: Tam Coc & Mua Cave
venues.note: The Tam Coc river boats drift through three caves and golden paddies, while a climb of some 500 steps to the Mua Cave viewpoint delivers the definitive panorama over the karst valley. The signature photograph of northern Vietnam.

venues.name: Bai Dinh Pagoda
venues.note: The largest Buddhist temple complex in Vietnam, a vast modern hillside of halls, a corridor lined with 500 stone arhats and the tallest bronze Buddha in Southeast Asia. Often paired with Trang An on the same Ninh Binh circuit.

venues.name: Perfume Pagoda
venues.note: A revered pilgrimage of shrines set in a limestone massif, reached by a rowed boat along the Yen stream and then a cable car or hike to the sacred Huong Tich grotto. Loveliest and busiest during the spring festival; serene the rest of the year, about two hours from the city.

venues.name: Duong Lam ancient village
venues.note: A cluster of hamlets 50 km from Hanoi where 300- to 400-year-old laterite houses, communal halls and banyan-shaded gates preserve the northern delta village of another century. The first village in Vietnam granted national heritage status, a gentle, authentic day in the countryside.

venues.name: Mai Chau valley
venues.note: A wide green valley of rice terraces and White Thai stilt-house villages, ideal for cycling between hamlets and an overnight stay among the ethnic-minority communities. A soft, scenic introduction to the northern highlands, about four hours out.

venues.name: Ancient House at 87 Ma May
venues.note: A restored 19th-century merchant's tube-house open to visitors, its dim rooms and inner courtyard showing exactly how the Old Quarter's traders lived and worked. A five-minute masterclass in vernacular architecture in the heart of the lanes.

venues.name: Bach Ma Temple
venues.note: The oldest temple in the Old Quarter, dedicated to the white horse spirit said to have guided the founding of the citadel, hushed and incense-dark amid the market bustle. A quiet detour most visitors miss.

venues.name: Vietnam Military History Museum
venues.note: The nation's flagship military museum, reopened in 2024 in a vast new campus, tracing centuries of resistance through aircraft, tanks and a soaring victory tower. Sweeping, modern and thorough for those drawn to the war years.

venues.name: Hanoi cooking class
venues.note: A guided morning at the market followed by a private hands-on class in pho, fresh spring rolls and bun cha, with vegetarian menus arranged in advance. A hands-on souvenir the whole family carries home.

venues.name: Ceramic Mosaic Mural along the Red River dyke
venues.note: A record-holding ceramic mural running several kilometres along the dyke road, telling Vietnamese history in tiny tiles. A colourful, offbeat stop en route to the Long Bien Bridge or Bat Trang.

venues.name: Tay Ho lakeside dining & sunset drinks
venues.note: West Lake's shore holds Hanoi's most relaxed fine dining and rooftop bars, the water turning gold as the city lights come up. The natural place for a slow, elegant evening away from Old Quarter's clamour.

venues.name: Workshop14
venues.note: The city's most exciting new bar, local ingredients, serious technique, and a place on Asia's list within months of opening.

venues.name: The Hudson Rooms
venues.note: A dazzling bar inside the Three-Key Capella, 1920s glamour and cocktails to match the setting.

venues.name: The Haflington
venues.note: A cocktail bar staged like a night in a European museum, the first Vietnamese bar ever to break Asia's top 50.
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Bars 2024 (No. 50), Vietnam's first top-50 bar

venues.name: Nê Cocktail Bar
venues.note: The bar that put Hanoi on the map, birthplace of the celebrated 'Phở' cocktail, distilling the city into a glass.

venues.name: Bamboo Bar, Sofitel Legend Metropole
venues.note: A poolside Indochine bar in the city's grande dame, a rediscovered wartime air-raid shelter lies just beneath it.
credentials: Inside the Metropole, a MICHELIN One-Key, Forbes Five-Star landmark hotel

venues.name: Top of Hanoi, Lotte Hotel
venues.note: An open-air perch on the 67th floor of the Lotte Tower, the highest, widest view over the whole city.
credentials: Hanoi's highest rooftop bar, atop the 65-storey Lotte Tower
